DATED: 16/06/2023  IN THE HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD  R/CRIMINAL MISC.APPLICATION NO. 12516 of 2013 ==========================================================
 IMRANBHAI SALIMBHAI SAMJANI & 3 other(s)
 Versus  STATE OF GUJARAT & 1 other(s)
==========================================================
Appearance:
MR KUNAL S SHAH(5282) for the Applicant(s) No. 1,2,3,4 NOTICE SERVED BY DS for the Respondent(s) No. 2 MR.THIRTHRAJ PANDYA, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1 ==========================================================
 CORAM:HONOURABLE MS. JUSTICE S.V. PINTO  Date : 16/06/2023  ORAL ORDER

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF GUJARAT AT AHMEDABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Though served, none appears for and on behalf of the respondent no.2 to assist this court in the present application.

1. By way of the present application, the applicants have prayed to quash and set aside the FIR being CR No.II-23 of 2013 registered with Datha Police Station, Dist. Bhavnagar for the offence punishable under Sections 498A, 323, 504, 506(2) and 114 of the Indian Penal Code and has further prayed to stay the further proceedings thereof till final disposal of this application.

2. Heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties.
3.

It is submitted by the learned advocate for the applicants that the impugned complaint has been filed with a view to wreck R/CR.MA/12516/2013 ORDER DATED: 16/06/2023 vengeance and to settle scores in view of the fact that the daughter of the applicant No.1's has filed a complaint against the family members of the respondent No.2 and therefore, as a counterblast, the respondent No.2 has lodged the impugned complaint, which is nothing but a sheer abuse of process of law.

That,
looking to the FIR, it appears that all the family members of the respondent No.2 had gone to the house of the applicant No.1 and the incident as stated above had taken place and they abused and demanded an amount of Rs.50,000/- from the complainant.

That, infact the applicant No.4 is a minor girl aged about 14 years, hence, the allegation made in the FIR that the applicant No.1 wants Imranbhai Salimbhai Samjani vs State Of Gujarat on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/173366599/
1 to get her married with her, is quite improbable.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: That, the respondent No.2 has initiated the proceedings after the daughter of the applicant No.1 filed the complaint and looking to the complaint the applicant No.4 is a minor and she has nothing to do with the allegations levelled in the impugned FIR and she is not aware about any of the incidents.

That, the so called incident, as stated in the FIR, had taken place on 5.6.2013 and the impugned complaint is lodged on 5.7.2013 i.e.
after 1 month and there is no explanation offered by the respondent R/CR.MA/12516/2013 ORDER DATED: 16/06/2023 No.2 for filing the complaint after such a long delay.
Hence, the learned advocate appearing for the applicants has requested to quash and set aside the impugned complaint.
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent-State has opposed to grant of present application considering the nature and gravity of the offence.

5. Having heard learned advocates appearing for the respective parties and having considered the facts of the case,it appears that on 04.07.2014, learned advocate for the applicants stated before the bar that the matter is settled between the parties and the parties have taken a divorce.

It further appears from the record that on 21.04.2023, learned advocate for the applicants has further reiterated the said version and has also submitted that the original maintenance application has been withdrawn by the wife.

Not only that, this court had issued rule to the respondent no.2 on 04.07.2014 and about 9 years have passed but the respondent no.2 has not appeared before this court by herself or through her learned advocate nor has not made any arrangement for her appearance before this court.
R/CR.MA/12516/2013 ORDER DATED: 16/06/2023 6.
If the allegations made in the FIR are considered and taken at face value and accepted in entirely they do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

Moreover,
there is no explanation whatsoever regarding the long delay in filing the FIR and the allegations do not constitute a cognizable offence and it prima facie appears that no cognizable case is made out against the accused therein.
7.

Thus, considering the allegations made in the complaint which are of a vague nature and here all no reasons for delay in filing of the complaint and the aforesaid situation, it appears that as per the statement of the learned advocate for the applicants the dispute has been settled and even though the respondent no.2 was served has not made any arrangement for her appearance before this court,
thus in the interest of justice this court deems it fit that the further criminal proceedings in relation to the impugned FIR against the applicants is not required to be proceeded further.
Hence, to secure the ends of justice, the impugned FIR and other consequential proceedings are required to be quashed and set aside in the exercise of powers conferred under Section 482 of the Code.
Resultantly, this application is allowed.

The impugned FIR being C.R.No. II-23 of 2013 registered with Datha Police Station, Dist. Bhavnagar as well as other consequential proceedings are hereby quashed and set aside qua the present applicants herein.
Accordingly, Rule is made absolute.
